title: On the quasi-continuum approximation of some localized patterns in the FPUT lattice
authors: Su Yang, Wenrong Sun, Lei Liu, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis
abstract: In the present work, we present a number of localized wave patterns that are theoretically analyzed and   numerically illustrated to be observable within the   widely applicable paradigm of the FPUT lattice. In particular, we derive a modified KdV equation from the FPUT lattice, which admits a variety of localized waves including these exact rational solutions representing rogue-wave profiles, solitons and breathers on the top of not only homogeneous,   but also periodic elliptic function traveling-wave background. We utilize these exact solutions of the modified KdV reduction to construct consistent initial conditions for the FPUT lattice and perform time stepping of the latter. Relevant comparisons between these numerical solutions of the FPUT lattice and their associated analytical counterparts have been conducted to demonstrate good performance of the derived modified KdV reduction in approximating distinct localized wave structures from the FPUT lattice.   This approach paves the way for importing a number of   quasi-continuum waveforms to the FPUT lattice and the   potential associated physical experiments, including recent   ones in mechanical metamaterials.
summary: This paper investigates localized wave phenomena on the FPUT lattice by employing a quasi-continuum approximation derived from the modified KdV equation. By using exact solutions of the mKdV equation to initialize the discrete lattice, the authors demonstrate that this reduction accurately models various structures like solitons and rogue waves across different background states. This methodology provides a powerful tool for studying wave dynamics in nonlinear lattices.
main_problem: The work analyzes localized wave patterns, such as rogue waves, solitons, and breathers, that can exist within the dynamics of the FPUT lattice.
main_result: The study successfully demonstrates that exact solutions derived from the modified KdV equation can be used to construct initial conditions for the FPUT lattice, showing good quantitative agreement between numerical simulations and analytical predictions.
method: A quasi-continuum approximation is employed by deriving a reduced integrable equation (mKdV) from the discrete FPUT lattice model. The exact solutions of this continuum equation are then mapped back to initialize and validate time evolution on the discrete lattice.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou (FPUT) lattice, governed by a nonlinear chain interaction potential. This discrete model is approximated by the continuous modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) equation under specific assumptions ($K_3=0$).
key_observables: Rogue-wave profiles, solitons, breathers, and the relative $L_\infty$ error ($\epsilon(t)$) quantifying the agreement between numerical FPUT dynamics and analytical mKdV solutions.
important_parameters: The smallness parameter $\epsilon \ll 1$, which governs the validity of the multi-scale expansion; and elliptic moduli ($k$) used to define various background wave states (snoidal, dnoidal, cnoidal).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes $K_3=0$ ($ eta$-FPUT model) for the reduction to mKdV, and relies on formal smallness parameters $\epsilon \ll 1$ for the continuum approximation.
figures_summary: Figures compare numerical FPUT dynamics initialized via the method against analytical second-order rational solutions; other figures plot the relative $L_\infty$ error across different solution orders and background types (e.g., dark breathers on snoidal backgrounds).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the mKdV reduction from the FPUT lattice, then utilizing exact mKdV solutions to set initial conditions for the discrete system. It systematically tests this approach by examining localized waves—solitons, breathers, and rogue waves—on various background states (homogeneous, snoidal, dnoidal, cnoidal).
why_interesting: This work bridges the gap between continuum integrable models (like mKdV) and discrete physical systems (FPUT lattice), a common theme in nonlinear physics relevant to understanding wave propagation in structured materials.
